chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 489: The Cost of Freedom — Grief That Can’t Be Traded
chapter_meta_description: The Second Spirit is gone. Li Huowang, Bai Lingmiao, and Li Sui each mourn in silence, while the village struggles with grain shortages and brutal training. A quiet, devastating chapter on emotional collateral.
og_title: The Quiet After the Storm — Chapter 489 of Dao Gui Yi Xian
og_description: No rituals, no monsters — just a father hugging his daughter who doesn’t understand why the person she’s waiting for won’t come back.
twitter_title: The Second Spirit is gone, and nobody knows how to say goodbye.
twitter_description: Li Huowang got what he wanted, but the emotional bill came due: a pair of red shoes, a half-eaten wild dog, and a silence that lasts all night.

lore_anchors.definition: In Northeastern Chinese folk mediumship (跳大神, *tiao dashen*), the Second Spirit is a silent assistant to the Lead Spirit, often acting as a vessel or spiritual partner. In this novel, she has her own will and attachments, making her loss more than a ritual cost.

A person’s natural lifespan, which can be harvested, stored, and traded as a tangible resource in the Dao-Twisted World. The jade token Lian Zhibei receives can be exchanged for “untainted” (无垢) lifespan.

A simple steamed bun made from refined wheat flour. In pre-modern China, white flour was a luxury, and the promise of a white-flour lunch was a powerful incentive for laborers — here, it’s the only thing keeping the exhausted militiamen from quitting.

cultural_notes_faq.a: The Second Spirit is a silent assistant in Chinese folk mediumship — a spiritual partner who shares the medium’s pain and presence. In this novel, she was attached to Bai Lingmiao and had her own personality and attachments.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did the Second Spirit disappear?
cultural_notes_faq.a: She was driven away along with all the other spirits that were controlling Bai Lingmiao. The ritual that freed Bai Lingmiao could not distinguish between harmful spirits and the one who was like a sister to her.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Li Huowang so guilty?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He achieved his goal of freeing Bai Lingmiao, but he didn’t know it would cost the Second Spirit’s existence. He spends the whole chapter asking himself whether he would have made the same choice if he had known.

A person’s natural lifespan, which can be harvested, stored, and traded in the Dao-Twisted World as a tangible resource. Lian Zhibei receives a jade token that can be exchanged for untainted yang-life.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Gao Zhijian drawing on the ground?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He’s trying to explain that he has money from his past, but he can’t find the words — possibly because of trauma or a secret he’s not ready to share. The drawing is his way of communicating when speech fails him.
